message.content: {"answer": "C", "option_text": "Right hemidiaphragm elevation due to hepatomegaly", "reason": "Visual inspection of Figure 1 reveals marked elevation of the right hemidiaphragm with a smooth, intact contour and no evidence of subdiaphragmatic air or fluid levels that would suggest an abscess. The left hemidiaphragm appears normal without scalloping, ruling out lymphangioma. There is no retrocardiac mass or air-fluid level to support hiatal hernia, and pleural spaces are clear, excluding bilateral effusion. While phrenic nerve paralysis causes elevation, the specific combination of isolated right-sided elevation with a preserved dome shape in the absence of other neuromuscular signs is classically associated with subdiaphragmatic mass effect, specifically hepatomegaly pushing the diaphragm upward. Automated tools failed to identify this structural etiology (guided by t000003), necessitating reliance on direct pixel verification of the diaphragmatic contour and adjacent anatomy."}
